qua, che mi pesa assai. Sir John, se voi: here, which weighs heavily on me. Sir John, if you wish

qua, che mi pesa assai. Sir John, se voi.meaning: you wish / you want (2nd plur. present)

qua, che mi pesa assai. Sir John, se voi: Ford (disguised as Signor Fontana) presents the heavy purse of gold coins to Falstaff, framing the bribe as a physical burden he needs assistance carrying.

aiutarmi a portarlo....meaning: to carry it / bear it (portare + clitic lo)

Continuing the mock-polite euphemism: 'portarlo' (to carry it) refers to taking the heavy sack of gold coins off Ford's hands.
Con gran piacer... non so,: With great pleasure... I do not know,
Falstaff eagerly accepts the gold while putting on an air of modest puzzlement as to why a stranger is offering such lavish bounty.
truly, by what merit of mine, sir...
Falstaff fishes for compliments and clarification while feigning humility ('per qual mio merito' - by what merit of mine).
I will tell it to you.

Ve lo dirò..meaning: to you (pronominal form of vi before lo)
I will tell / I will say (1st sing. future)

Double clitic pronoun construction 've lo' (vi + lo: 'to you it') followed by the future of 'dire'. Ford prepares to spin his fabricated tale.
C'è a Windsor, una dama, bella e leggiad: There is in Windsor a lady, very beautiful and graceful.
Ford begins describing his wife Alice under the guise of an ardent secret admirer, ironically singing her praises to the very man who wrote to seduce her.
Si chiama Alice; è moglie di un certo Fo: Her name is Alice; she is wife of a certain Ford.

Si chiama Alice; è moglie di un certo Fo.meaning: her name is / she is called

Si chiama Alice; è moglie di un certo Fo: Peak dramatic irony: Ford refers to himself in the third person as 'un certo Ford' ('a certain Ford'), testing Falstaff's reaction.
Io l'amo e lei non m'ama; le scrivo, non: I love her and she does not love me; I write to her, she does not answer;

Io l'amo e lei non m'ama; le scrivo, non.meaning: she does not love me (non + clitic mi + amare)
I write to her (clitic le + scrivere)

Io l'amo e lei non m'ama; le scrivo, non: Ford recites a string of Petrarchan antitheses ('amo / non m'ama', 'scrivo / non risponde') mimicking the traditional complaints of an unrequited courtly lover.
la guardo, non mi guarda; la cerco e si: I look at her, she does not look at me; I seek her and she hides.

la guardo, non mi guarda; la cerco e si.meaning: I look at / gaze upon (1st sing. present)
I seek / look for (1st sing. present)

la guardo, non mi guarda; la cerco e si: Balanced rhythmic parallelisms ('guardo / non mi guarda', 'cerco / si nasconde') continuing Ford's complaint of Alice's cold aloofness.
Per lei sprecai tesori, gittai doni su d: For her I squandered treasures, threw gifts upon gifts,

Per lei sprecai tesori, gittai doni su d.meaning: I squandered / wasted (1st sing. passato remoto)
I threw / cast (archaic passato remoto of gettare/gittare)

Per lei sprecai tesori, gittai doni su d: Passato remoto verbs 'sprecai' and 'gittai' (poetic/archaic form of 'gettai') convey the vast fortunes Fontana claims to have showered upon Alice in vain.
escogitai, tremando, il vol delle occasi: I devised, trembling, the flight of opportunities.

escogitai, tremando, il vol delle occasi.meaning: I devised / concocted (1st sing. passato remoto)

escogitai, tremando, il vol delle occasi: High poetic diction: 'il vol delle occasioni' refers to seizing fleeting moments of opportunity (poetic apocope 'vol' from 'volo').
Ahimè! tutto fu vano! Rimasi sulle scale: Alas! all was in vain! I remained on the stairs,

Ahimè! tutto fu vano! Rimasi sulle scale.meaning: I remained / stayed (1st sing. passato remoto)

Ahimè! tutto fu vano! Rimasi sulle scale: 'Rimasi sulle scale' literally means left stranded outside on the staircase, shut out from the lady's chambers.

negletto, a bocca asciutta, cantando un.meaning: empty-handed / left high and dry / dry-mouthed

negletto, a bocca asciutta, cantando un: Vivid Italian idiom 'a bocca asciutta' (literally 'with dry mouth', meaning left completely empty-handed or ungratified), contrasting with the lofty artifice of singing a madrigal.
L'amor, l'amor che non ci dà mai tregue: Love, love which never gives us respite
Falstaff pontificates on love with a philosophical adage. 'Non dar tregue' means granting no peace or truce.
finché la vita strugge: as long as life burns away

finché la vita strugge.meaning: consumes / melts / wastes away (3rd sing. present)

finché la vita strugge: 'Struggere' is a classic poetic Italian verb meaning to melt, consume, or waste away with ardent passion or time.
Falstaff introduces the well-known Renaissance emblem comparing love to a shadow, which Boito borrows directly from Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor (Act II, Scene 2).
Score cue embeds Ford's name as he jumps in to complete the proverb ('Love like a shadow flies when substance love pursues; pursuing that that flies, and flying what pursues').
Falstaff chips in the rhyming verb: the shadow pursues whoever flees from it.
Ford chimes in with the second half of the chiasmus.
Falstaff concludes the reciprocal proverb: whoever chases the shadow finds it fleeing from them.
FORD E FALSTAFF: Score cue indicating Ford and Falstaff singing simultaneously in mock-serious lyric harmony.
Ford and Falstaff unite their voices in a shared lyrical sigh over the elusive, paradoxical nature of love.
E questo madrigale l'ho appreso a prezzo: And this madrigal I learned at the price of gold.

E questo madrigale l'ho appreso a prezzo.meaning: of gold / a heavy price (di + oro)

E questo madrigale l'ho appreso a prezzo: Ford wryly remarks that this courtly lesson cost him an exorbitant fortune in gifts that bore no fruit ('a prezzo d'oro').
Quest'è il destin fatale del misero amat: This is the fateful destiny of the wretched lover.
Falstaff sums up Fontana's plight with patronizing sympathy, feeling immensely smug in his own supposed mastery of romance.
Essa non vi diè mai luogo a lusinghe?: Did she never give you room for hope?

Essa non vi diè mai luogo a lusinghe?.meaning: gave (poetic 3rd sing. passato remoto of dare)

Essa non vi diè mai luogo a lusinghe?: Poetic 3rd sing. passato remoto 'diè' (= diede). The idiom 'dar luogo a lusinghe' means to give encouragement or ground for romantic hopes.
Ford's blunt monosyllable underscores his wife's incorruptible chastity.
FALSTAFF Ma infin, perché v'aprite a me?: FALSTAFF: But in the end, why do you open your heart to me?

FALSTAFF Ma infin, perché v'aprite a me?.meaning: in the end / after all (apocope of infine)

FALSTAFF Ma infin, perché v'aprite a me?: Falstaff gets straight to the point: what does Fontana want from him? 'Aprirsi a' means to open one's heart or confide in someone.
Ve lo dirò:: I will tell it to you:
Ford repeats his introductory formula before detailing his bizarre proposal.
voi siete un gentiluomo prode, arguto, f: you are a gentleman valiant, witty, eloquent,
Ford flatters Falstaff with an elevated triad of courtly adjectives ('prode, arguto, facondo'), inflating the old knight's boundless ego.
voi siete un uom di guerra, voi siete un: you are a man of war, you are a man of the world...

voi siete un uom di guerra, voi siete un.meaning: man of the world / worldly man

voi siete un uom di guerra, voi siete un: Parallelism contrasting military valor ('uom di guerra') with worldly social polish ('uom di mondo').
Falstaff grunts with self-satisfied delight at being called a man of war and a man of the world.
Non vi adulo, e quello è un sacco di mon: I do not flatter you, and that is a sack of coins:
Ford seals his verbal flattery with the irresistible enticement of hard currency ('un sacco di monete').
spendetele! spendetele! sì, spendete e s: spend them! spend them! yes, spend and squander

spendetele! spendetele! sì, spendete e s.meaning: to spend lavishly / squander money without restraint

spendetele! spendetele! sì, spendete e s: Alliterative idiom 'spendere e spandere' (to spend lavishly and throw money around), reinforced by urgent repeated imperatives.
tutto il mio patrimonio! Siate ricco e f: all my estate! Be rich and happy!
Ford urges Falstaff to squander Fontana's entire fortune on himself, setting up the quid pro quo.
Ma, in contraccambio, chiedo che conquis: But, in return, I ask that you conquer Alice!

Ma, in contraccambio, chiedo che conquis.meaning: you conquer / win over (2nd plur. present subjunctive)

Ma, in contraccambio, chiedo che conquis: The heart of the bargain: Ford asks Falstaff to seduce Alice. Subjunctive 'conquistiate' follows the governing verb of request 'chiedo che'.
Strana ingiunzion!: Falstaff is taken aback by Fontana's bizarre request: why pay another man to seduce the woman Fontana himself covets?
Mi spiego: quella crudel beltà: I explain myself: that cruel beauty

Mi spiego: quella crudel beltà.meaning: I explain myself / let me explain
beauty / fair woman (poetic apocope of bellezza)

Mi spiego: quella crudel beltà: Ford explains his cunning rationale using poetic romance vocabulary ('crudel beltà').
sempre è vissuta in grande fede di casti: has always lived in great reputation of chastity.
'In fede di castità' signifies possessing an established reputation for unblemished chastity.
La sua virtù importuna m'abbarbagliava g: Her troublesome virtue dazzled my eyes,

La sua virtù importuna m'abbarbagliava g.meaning: dazzled me / blinded me (clitic mi + abbarbagliare)

La sua virtù importuna m'abbarbagliava g: 'Abbarbagliare' means to dazzle or blind someone with overpowering glare; Ford portrays Alice's uprightness as a blinding obstacle.
la bella inespugnabile dicea: «Guai se m: the impregnable beauty said: «Woe if you touch me!»
Poetic imperfect 'dicea' (= diceva). 'Inespugnabile' uses the vocabulary of military siege for female chastity. 'Guai se...' expresses a fierce warning.
Ma se voi l'espugnate, poi, posso anch'i: But if you breach it, then I too can hope:

Ma se voi l'espugnate, poi, posso anch'i.meaning: you conquer / take by storm (2nd plur. present)

Ma se voi l'espugnate, poi, posso anch'i: Carrying through the fortress siege metaphor: if Falstaff breaches her defenses ('l'espugnate'), the stronghold will no longer be impenetrable.
da fallo nasce fallo e allor... Che ve n: from fault arises fault and then... What do you think of it?

da fallo nasce fallo e allor... Che ve n.meaning: what do you think of it? / how does it seem to you?

da fallo nasce fallo e allor... Che ve n: A cynical maxim ('da fallo nasce fallo' - one lapse in virtue leads to another). Once Alice yields to Falstaff, Fontana believes she can be persuaded to yield to him as well.
Prima di tutto, senza complimenti, messe: First of all, without ceremonies, sir,

Prima di tutto, senza complimenti, messe.meaning: without ceremonies / without standing on formality

Prima di tutto, senza complimenti, messe: Falstaff sweeps aside polite formalities ('senza complimenti') in his eagerness to take the money.
accetto il sacco. E poi (fede di cavalie: I accept the sack. And then (knight's faith:

accetto il sacco. E poi (fede di cavalie.meaning: knight's word / on my honor as a knight

accetto il sacco. E poi (fede di cavalie: Comic irony: Falstaff pledges his knightly honor ('fede di cavaliere') to act as a paid seducer, after having spent Act 1 Scene 1 denouncing 'onore' as useless breath.
qua la mano!) farò le vostre brame sazie: shake hands!) I will satisfy your desires.

qua la mano!) farò le vostre brame sazie.meaning: shake hands! / give me your hand!
I will make / render (1st sing. future)

qua la mano!) farò le vostre brame sazie: 'Qua la mano' seals the pact with a handshake. 'Far sazie le brame' means to fully satisfy longings or appetites.
You, the wife of Ford shall possess.

Voi, la moglie di Ford possederete..meaning: you will possess / have (2nd plur. future)

Falstaff makes a direct, brazen promise to Fontana: 'You shall possess Ford's wife.' The dramatic irony is devastating, as Fontana is Ford.
Grazie!: Ford's exclamation of thanks is loaded with bitter sarcasm and boiling indignation.

Io son già molto innanzi.meaning: to be far along / well advanced

Io son già molto innanzi: Falstaff boasts that he has already made enormous headway with Alice, unable to keep his triumph to himself.
(non c'è ragion ch'io taccia con voi) :: (there is no reason for me to keep silent with you) : in half an hour she will be in my arms.

(non c'è ragion ch'io taccia con voi) :.meaning: I keep silent / hold my tongue (1st sing. present subjunctive)

(non c'è ragion ch'io taccia con voi) :: Falstaff casually drops a massive revelation: Alice will be in his arms within thirty minutes. Subjunctive 'ch'io taccia' follows the negative expression 'non c'è ragion che'.
Ford is dumbfounded, scarcely able to believe his ears.
Alice. Essa mandò dianzi una... confiden: Alice. She sent just now a... confidante
Falstaff identifies Alice and mentions the go-between (Mistress Quickly), relishing the apparent success of his charm.
per dirmi che quel tanghero di suo marit: to tell me that that boor of her husband is away
Falstaff hurls the colorful Italian insult 'tanghero' (coarse boor / oaf) at Ford right to his face, oblivious of who he is talking to.
Falstaff reveals the precise rendezvous hours ('dalle due alle tre'), which Alice and Quickly had calculated for Ford's routine absence.

Lo conoscete?.meaning: you know / are acquainted with (2nd plur. present)

Lo conoscete?: Ford asks with tense restraint whether Falstaff actually knows Master Ford personally.
Il diavolo: Falstaff starts an extravagant, colorful curse against the husband.
se lo porti all'inferno con Menelao suo: take him to hell with Menelaus his ancestor!

se lo porti all'inferno con Menelao suo.meaning: carry off / take (3rd sing. present subjunctive)

se lo porti all'inferno con Menelao suo: Optative subjunctive curse ('se lo porti'). Calling Menelaus (the archetypal cuckolded husband of Helen of Troy) Ford's ancestor ('suo avolo') stamps Ford as an inherent, destined cuckold.
Vedrai! Te lo cornifico netto! se mi fra: You will see! I will cuckold him clean for you! If he bothers me

Vedrai! Te lo cornifico netto! se mi fra.meaning: I cuckold / give horns to (1st sing. present)
disturbs / disrupts / gets in the way of (3rd sing. present)

Vedrai! Te lo cornifico netto! se mi fra: Ethic dative 'te lo cornifico' ('I'll cuckold him for you'). 'Cornificare' is the quintessential Italian verb for cuckolding a husband. 'Netto' signifies doing it thoroughly and without fail.
gli sparo una girandola di botte sulle c: I will loose a pinwheel of blows upon his horns!

gli sparo una girandola di botte sulle c.meaning: I loose / fire off (1st sing. present)

gli sparo una girandola di botte sulle c: Vivid comedic bravado: Falstaff threatens to rain down a spinning Catherine wheel of blows ('una girandola di botte') directly on Ford's horns.
Quel messer Ford è un bue! Un bue! Te lo: That Master Ford is an ox! An ox! I will dupe him for you,

Quel messer Ford è un bue! Un bue! Te lo.meaning: I dupe / hoodwink / mock (1st sing. present)

Quel messer Ford è un bue! Un bue! Te lo: 'Bue' (ox) is an Italian metaphor for a cuckold and slow-witted dunce. 'Corbellare' means to hoodwink, mock, or fool completely.
vedrai! Ma è tardi. Aspettami qua. Vado: you will see! But it is late. Wait for me here. I go to make myself handsome.

vedrai! Ma è tardi. Aspettami qua. Vado.meaning: wait for me! (imperative aspettate/aspetta + clitic mi)
to groom oneself / dress up / spruce oneself up

vedrai! Ma è tardi. Aspettami qua. Vado: 'Farsi bello' is an expressive Italian idiom for sprucing oneself up and dressing in one's finest. Falstaff exits, leaving Ford to his volcanic fury.
È sogno o realtà?... Due rami enormi: Is it a dream or reality?... Two enormous branches
Opening of Ford's celebrated jealousy monologue. He questions his senses before envisioning 'due rami enormi' (two giant branched horns) sprouting from his forehead.
Ford feels his own forehead in horror, convinced that the visible antlers of cuckoldry are actively growing upon his head.
È un sogno? Mastro Ford! Mastro Ford! Do: Is it a dream? Master Ford! Master Ford! Are you asleep?

È un sogno? Mastro Ford! Mastro Ford! Do.meaning: are you sleeping? / do you sleep? (2nd sing. present)

È un sogno? Mastro Ford! Mastro Ford! Do: Ford addresses himself in the second person by his civic title 'Mastro Ford', rebuking his own complacency.
Svegliati! Su! Ti desta!: Wake up! Come on! Rouse yourself!
Urgent, staccato reflexive imperatives ('Svegliati!', 'Ti desta!') as Ford spurs himself into fury and defensive action.
Tua moglie sgarra e mette in mal assetto: Your wife strays and throws into disarray

Tua moglie sgarra e mette in mal assetto.meaning: to throw into disorder / bring to ruin / put into disarray

Tua moglie sgarra e mette in mal assetto: 'Sgarrare' means to step out of bounds or transgress. 'Mettere in mal assetto' is an idiom meaning to throw into complete disorder or disrepute.
l'onore tuo, la tua casa ed il tuo letto: your honor, your house, and your bed!
Tricolon of domestic bourgeois values ('l'onore tuo, la tua casa ed il tuo letto') desecrated by Alice's presumed infidelity.
L'ora è fissata, tramato l'inganno;: The hour is set, the deception plotted;
Pithy elliptical clauses with past participles ('fissata', 'tramato') conveying relentless impending betrayal.
Verbs 'gabbare' (to fool or dupe) and 'truffare' (to swindle) evoke the bitter realization of being a humiliated laughingstock.
E poi diranno: Ford imagines the cruel verdict of society and gossiping neighbors.
che un marito geloso è un insensato!: that a jealous husband is a madman!
Ford vents his bitterness at the common perception that jealous husbands are irrational ('un insensato'), when in his case his jealousy is dead right.
Già dietro a me nomi d'infame conio: Already behind me names of infamous stamp
Metaphor 'nomi d'infame conio' refers to insults freshly minted like debased coins to brand a cuckolded husband.
whistle as they pass; mockery murmurs.
Auditory imagery of hissing and whispering ('fischian', 'mormora') evoking public derision following Ford down the street.
O matrimonio, inferno!: Ford denounces the institution of marriage as pure hell, leading into his condemnation of womankind.
Donna: demonio!: Succinct, furious rhyming exclamation ('matrimonio, inferno / Donna: demonio!').
Nella lor moglie abbian fede i babbei!: In their wife let simpletons have faith!

Nella lor moglie abbian fede i babbei!.meaning: let them have (apocope of abbiano, 3rd plur. present subjunctive)

Nella lor moglie abbian fede i babbei!: Jussive subjunctive 'abbian fede' (let them trust). 'Babbeo' is an expressive term for an easily gullible dupe.

Affiderei.meaning: I would entrust / trust (1st sing. conditional)

Affiderei: Conditional 'affiderei' launches a series of absurd, exaggerated hypotheticals borrowed from Shakespeare (Ford's soliloquy in Merry Wives II.2).
la mia birra a un tedesco,: First comparison of reckless trust: leaving beer unguarded with a thirsty German.
tutto il mio desco: 'Desco' is a literary term for the dinner table or banquet board.
a un olandese lurco,: 'Lurco' is an archaism/Dantean poetic term for a ravenous, gluttonous eater.
la mia bottiglia d'acquavite a un turco,: my bottle of spirits to a Turk,
Another paradoxical risk: entrusting strong liquor ('acquavite') to a Turk (borrowed from Shakespeare's 'an Irishman with my aqua-vitae bottle').
non mia moglie a sé stessa. O laida sort: not my wife to herself. O foul destiny!
The punchline: Ford would trust all those treasures before trusting his wife alone with herself. 'Laida' means disgusting, vile, or foul.
Quella brutta parola in cor mi torna:: That ugly word returns to my heart:
'Quella brutta parola' echoes Falstaff's taunting mention of 'le corna'.
«Le corna!» Bue! Capron! le fusa torte!: Climax of cuckold imagery. 'Bue' and 'capron' are horned animals symbolizing cuckolds; 'fusa torte' (literally twisted spinning spindles) is an ancient Tuscan idiom for crooked horns.
Ah! «le corna! le corna!»: Ford cries out in anguish as the obsessive nightmare of cuckoldry consumes him.
Ma non mi sfuggirai! no! sozzo, reo,: But you shall not escape me! No! filthy, guilty,

Ma non mi sfuggirai! no! sozzo, reo,.meaning: you will escape / elude (2nd sing. future)

Ma non mi sfuggirai! no! sozzo, reo,: Ford pivots from despair to thirst for revenge, addressing the absent Falstaff. 'Sozzo' (foul/disgusting) and 'reo' (wicked/culpable) target Falstaff's vices.
dannato epicureo!: Boito's translation of Shakespeare's insult 'damned Epicurean rascal'—referring to one who lives solely for gluttonous and carnal pleasures.
Prima li accoppio: First I will trap them together

Prima li accoppio.meaning: I couple / pair together / trap together (1st sing. present)

Prima li accoppio: Ford resolves to let the two lovers come together ('li accoppio') so he can catch them red-handed.
e poi li colgo. Io scoppio!: and then I catch them. I am bursting!
Rhyme 'accoppio / scoppio'. 'Li colgo' means catching them in the act; 'io scoppio' conveys Ford's inner explosion of jealous rage.
Vendicherò l'affronto!: A resolute vow of vengeance sealing Ford's transition into furious determination.

Laudata sempre sia.meaning: let it be (3rd sing. present subjunctive)

Laudata sempre sia: Ford adopts liturgical language ('Laudata sempre sia' - Praised be forever), perversely elevating his jealousy to a sacred blessing.
in the depth of my heart, jealousy.
The crowning climax of Ford's monologue, singing a hymn of praise to jealousy for having opened his eyes in time.
Here I am. I am ready.

Eccomi qua. Son pronto..meaning: here I am (presentative ecco + clitic mi)

Falstaff re-enters gorgeously preened and perfumed, creating an abrupt comedic contrast with Ford's tragic jealousy.
M'accompagnate un tratto?: Will you accompany me a little way?

M'accompagnate un tratto?.meaning: will you accompany me? (clitic mi + accompagnare)
a little way / a short distance

M'accompagnate un tratto?: 'Un tratto' idiomatically means a short distance. Falstaff genially asks Fontana to walk out with him.
I will set you on your way.

Vi metto sulla via..meaning: on the way / on the road

Ford's answer has chilling dramatic irony: 'I'll set you on your way' doubles as leading Falstaff straight to his doom.
Falstaff politely insists that Fontana go first ('Prima voi' - literally 'You first', meaning 'After you').
No, I am in my house.
Falstaff argues host etiquette: since this inn is his current lodgings, the guest must walk out first.

Passate..meaning: pass through / go ahead (2nd plur. imperative)

Falstaff gestures courteously toward the doorway.
Ford counters with equal exaggerated politeness, refusing to take precedence.
It is late. The appointment presses.
Falstaff stresses urgency: his romantic rendezvous ('l'appuntamento') with Alice cannot wait.

Non fate complimenti....meaning: to stand on ceremony / fuss over etiquette

'Non fate complimenti' is the standard Italian expression for 'don't stand on ceremony'.
Well then; let us pass together.

Ebben; passiamo insieme..meaning: let us pass / go through (1st plur. imperative)

Resolving the comic doorway stalemate, Falstaff and Ford link arms and pass through the door together, bringing the scene to a triumphant close.
